-weak-Perron linear numeration systems is finite.
+Let \(U\) be a strictly increasing, eventually linearly recurrent sequence
+of positive place values with a finite canonical digit language. Every
+infinite multiple context-free sublanguage contains an injective
+synchronized orbit whose values return modulo each integer coprime to the
+trailing recurrence coefficient. These returns give prime-support and
+scatteredness obstructions, including MCF-immunity of the prime and
+bounded-\(\Omega\) representation languages. For the intrinsic minimal
+tail recurrence, bounded prime support occurs on an infinite
+multiple context-free sublanguage if and only if the canonical language
+contains a synchronized ray with values \(cb^t\), where \(c\ge1\) and
+\(b\ge2\). In a standard greedy system whose minimal tail polynomial is
+the minimal polynomial of a weak Perron number \(\beta\), this is equivalent
+to integrality of some positive power of \(\beta\). Finally, a finite
+paired-loop cover converts slender context-free representations into
+recurrence sequences: Mignotte's common-value theorem then implies that a
+set represented by slender context-free languages in two multiplicatively
+independent weak-Perron systems is finite. Complete effective presentations
+also yield a computable cardinality bound.
 \end{abstract}

-The affine recurrence action turns one weak MCFL pumping family into a

+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension
-problem for context-free sequences discussed by Caucal and Le Gonidec
-\cite{CaucalLeGonidec2014}; this paper does not settle it. The weak pumping
-mechanism itself still supplies only one ray inside one infinite MCFL, and
-two representations of the same set may supply unrelated rays with no
-common values. It neither controls every sufficiently long word nor the
-whole canonical language. The slender-context-free theorem proved here
-escapes that ceiling only because the Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie
-classification replaces a single pumped orbit by a finite paired-loop cover
-of each full representation language. Mignotte's theorem then makes every
-pair of loop images have finite intersection. Retaining the individual
-recurrence shifts, spectral data, and effective Mignotte thresholds gives the
-cardinality bound in \Cref{thm:effective-slender-cfl-cardinality}, but not a
-closed bound in compact grammar-size parameters. This is a different global
-argument, not a strengthening of the weak MCFL pumping lemma.
+The affine recurrence action converts one synchronized pumping family into
+an injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Adic topology
+turns those returns into scatteredness and prime-support obstructions, while
+Evertse's quotient theorem and Schur's theorem identify the remaining
+bounded-support possibility as a geometric ray \(cb^t\). In standard
+weak-Perron greedy systems, the length squeeze classifies that possibility
+algebraically: it occurs if and only if a positive power of the weak Perron
+root is an integer.
 
-The Supplementary Information (Online Resource 1) contains the independent fixed-DFA density and
-regular Zeckendorf results. Keeping those comparisons outside the article
-leaves the main theorem chain centered on synchronized recurrence orbits
-and their arithmetic consequences.
+For slender context-free languages, a finite paired-loop cover supplies
+global control of every represented value. The same affine evaluation sends
+each loop to finitely many recurrence sequences, and dominant-root transfer
+followed by Mignotte's theorem gives the two-system Cobham finiteness result.
+Complete recurrence and loop data yield an effective cardinality bound. For
+the one-system geometric-ray problem, candidate verification is effective,
+but no uniform bound is known for the fan-out and block lengths of a smallest
+witness; this is the missing step toward a general decision procedure.

+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a

+\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}, which supplies one synchronized family.
+The stronger pumping property fails for general MCFLs
+\cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}. The substitution lemma
+of Duncan--Elder--Frenkel--Lyu controls every sufficiently marked long word
+but allows switchable tuples rather than one fixed simultaneous-power
+orbit \cite[Theorem~4.5]{DuncanElderFrenkelLiu2026}; that distinction is
+why the older weak lemma gives the matrix powers used here.
 
+Evertse's quotient theorem is the arithmetic input for the geometric-ray
+step \cite[Theorem~3]{Evertse1984}; later \(S\)-part estimates concern the
+size of the supported part of recurrence terms
+\cite{BugeaudEvertse2017}. Broughan supplies the ambient adic
+classifications \cite{Broughan2003}. Frougny's normalization theorem and
+the Bertrand and substitution literature provide the regular canonical
+interfaces for Pisot numeration
+\cite{Frougny1992,BruyereHansel1997,Fabre1995,FrougnySolomyak1992}.
+Charlier--Kreczman obtain the residue-class quotient limits underlying the
+weak-Perron length squeeze \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025};
+the prime-support and MCFL classification is the additional interface
+proved here.
+
+For the two-system result, the paired-loop classification is due to
+Latteux--Thierrin and Ilie
+\cite{LatteuxThierrin1983,Ilie1994,IlieRozenbergSalomaa2000}, and the
+common-value input is Mignotte's theorem
+\cite{Mignotte1978Intersection}. Albayrak--Bell's quantitative
+Cobham--Semenov theorem contains the regular integer-base specialization
+and gives a stronger explicit automaton bound there
+\cite[Theorems~1.1 and 4.1]{AlbayrakBell2023}. Regular Perron-substitutive
+and regular abstract-numeration cases lie in existing Cobham theory
+\cite[Theorem~1]{Durand2011CobhamSubstitutions}%
+\cite[Theorem~49]{CharlierLeroyRigo2013CobhamANS}. The contribution of
+Main Theorem C is the passage from genuinely nonregular slender
+context-free representation languages to recurrence sequences in
+weak-Perron positional systems.

+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension

-\cite{CaucalLeGonidec2014}; this paper does not settle it. The weak pumping

 \subsection{Organization}
 
-\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} begins with the context-free Zeckendorf

+Let \(U\) be a strictly increasing, eventually linearly recurrent sequence
+of positive place values with a finite canonical digit language. Every
+infinite multiple context-free sublanguage contains an injective
+synchronized orbit whose values return modulo each integer coprime to the
+trailing recurrence coefficient. These returns give prime-support and
+scatteredness obstructions, including MCF-immunity of the prime and

-\section{Conclusion and open interface}\label{sec:conclusion}
-
-The affine recurrence action turns one weak MCFL pumping family into a
-single injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Positive
-pumped length and uniqueness of canonical representation supply
-distinctness, while finite-group return times supply congruences. Applying
-Broughan's adic classifications to these orbits,
-together with the deleted-prime intrinsic derivative calculation, gives the
-scattered-set obstruction, the nonunit escape dichotomy, and prime and
-bounded-\(\Omega\) MCF-immunity.
-
-For the minimal tail recurrence, the residual bounded-support phenomenon
-has an exact structural form. It occurs on an infinite finite-fan-out MCFL
-if and only if the canonical language contains a synchronized ray with
-values \(cb^t\). Evertse's quotient theorem is used with an explicit
-prime-ideal norm bound to reduce a fixed-support recurrence to one
-characteristic root; Schur's theorem removes its polynomial factor. The
-ratio \(b\) uses only primes dividing the minimal tail constant. In a
-standard greedy linear numeration basis with weak-Perron recurrence, residue
-asymptotics and length thresholds show that such a ray exists exactly when
-some positive power of the weak Perron number is an integer. Alternating
-radices give an infinite family with nonintegral root \(\sqrt B\) and a
-regular ray of values \(B^t\).
-
-On the promised class of valid effectively presented regular canonical
-systems, with the minimal tail recurrence and threshold supplied or
-certified, positive promised instances can be enumerated and certified. The unresolved general step is not
-candidate verification but witness compression: no computable bound is
-known for the fan-out and word lengths of a smallest geometric synchronized
-scheme. DFA path compression does not preserve the associated affine
-recurrence matrices. Conversely, no reduction proving undecidability is
-known that also preserves unique canonical representation, the minimal tail
-recurrence, and the special digit-matrix form.
-Accordingly the general decision problem remains open, while the
-weak-Perron subclass has the exact algebraic classification above.
+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension
-problem for context-free sequences discussed by Caucal and Le Gonidec
-\cite{CaucalLeGonidec2014}; this paper does not settle it. The weak pumping
-mechanism itself still supplies only one ray inside one infinite MCFL, and
-two representations of the same set may supply unrelated rays with no
-common values. It neither controls every sufficiently long word nor the
-whole canonical language. The slender-context-free theorem proved here
-escapes that ceiling only because the Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie
-classification replaces a single pumped orbit by a finite paired-loop cover
-of each full representation language. Mignotte's theorem then makes every
-pair of loop images have finite intersection. Retaining the individual
-recurrence shifts, spectral data, and effective Mignotte thresholds gives the
-cardinality bound in \Cref{thm:effective-slender-cfl-cardinality}, but not a
-closed bound in compact grammar-size parameters. This is a different global
-argument, not a strengthening of the weak MCFL pumping lemma.
+The affine recurrence action converts one synchronized pumping family into
+an injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Adic topology
+turns those returns into scatteredness and prime-support obstructions, while
+Evertse's quotient theorem and Schur's theorem identify the remaining
+bounded-support possibility as a geometric ray \(cb^t\). In standard
+weak-Perron greedy systems, the length squeeze classifies that possibility
+algebraically: it occurs if and only if a positive power of the weak Perron
+root is an integer.
 
-The Supplementary Information (Online Resource 1) contains the independent fixed-DFA density and
-regular Zeckendorf results. Keeping those comparisons outside the article
-leaves the main theorem chain centered on synchronized recurrence orbits
-and their arithmetic consequences.
+For slender context-free languages, a finite paired-loop cover supplies
+global control of every represented value. The same affine evaluation sends
+each loop to finitely many recurrence sequences, and dominant-root transfer
+followed by Mignotte's theorem gives the two-system Cobham finiteness result.
+Complete recurrence and loop data yield an effective cardinality bound. For
+the one-system geometric-ray problem, candidate verification is effective,
+but no uniform bound is known for the fan-out and block lengths of a smallest
+witness; this is the missing step toward a general decision procedure.

-\subsection{Relation to prior work}\label{subsec:prior-work}
+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a
+prefix beyond the recurrence transient, every digit acts by an integral
+matrix, and every block matrix is invertible modulo integers coprime to the
+trailing coefficient. The weak pumping lemma of

+fixed blocks are raised to a common exponent. A common order of their
+matrices in a finite general linear group gives the returns in Main
+Theorem A; positive pumped length and canonical uniqueness give
+distinctness.

-\subsection{Relation to prior work}\label{subsec:prior-work}
+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a
+prefix beyond the recurrence transient, every digit acts by an integral
+matrix, and every block matrix is invertible modulo integers coprime to the
+trailing coefficient. The weak pumping lemma of
+Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami supplies one family in which finitely many
+fixed blocks are raised to a common exponent. A common order of their
+matrices in a finite general linear group gives the returns in Main
+Theorem A; positive pumped length and canonical uniqueness give
+distinctness.
 
-The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is classical, due to
-Hartmanis--Shank and Sch\"utzenberger
-\cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. Our language-theoretic input
-is exactly Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami's weak pumping lemma
-\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}: an infinite \(k\)-MCFL contains one family
-with \(2k\) fixed factors pumped by the same exponent. It says nothing
-about every sufficiently long word, and the corresponding strong pumping
-property fails for general MCFLs
-\cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}.
+These local returns place the orbit densely in the relevant congruence
+neighbourhoods. Broughan's adic classifications then yield the

+Cantor--Bendixson calculation after deleting the exceptional primes gives
+the alternative between new prime divisors and increasing exceptional
+valuations. In the unit case, the same returns also produce quotient
+congruences of arbitrary depth and a divisibility tree.

 \subsection{Organization}
 
-\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} begins with the context-free Zeckendorf
-motivation, develops the recurrent block action and synchronized MCFL orbit,
-proves the local-adic and prime-support consequences, establishes the
-geometric-ray characterization and its effective boundary, and concludes
-with the unit and weak-Perron specializations. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham}
-uses the global paired-loop classification to prove the separate two-system
-finiteness theorem, gives its effective cardinality refinement from complete
-presentations, and locates its nonregular contribution relative to existing
-Cobham results. \Cref{sec:conclusion} summarizes the proved scope and the

+\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} develops local rigidity from one synchronized
+orbit: the Zeckendorf model, affine recurrence action, prime-support
+obstructions, geometric-ray characterization, and weak-Perron
+classification. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham} develops global rigidity from a
+finite paired-loop cover and proves the two-system theorem and its effective
+cardinality refinement. Both branches use the passage
+\[
+  \text{structured word families}
+  \longrightarrow \text{affine matrix powers}
+  \longrightarrow \text{linear recurrences}
+  \longrightarrow \text{arithmetic rigidity}.

-candidate verification but witness compression: no computable bound is
-known for the fan-out and word lengths of a smallest geometric synchronized
-scheme. DFA path compression does not preserve the associated affine
-recurrence matrices. Conversely, no reduction proving undecidability is

+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension
-problem for context-free sequences discussed by Caucal and Le Gonidec
-\cite{CaucalLeGonidec2014}; this paper does not settle it. The weak pumping
-mechanism itself still supplies only one ray inside one infinite MCFL, and
-two representations of the same set may supply unrelated rays with no
-common values. It neither controls every sufficiently long word nor the
-whole canonical language. The slender-context-free theorem proved here
-escapes that ceiling only because the Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie
-classification replaces a single pumped orbit by a finite paired-loop cover
-of each full representation language. Mignotte's theorem then makes every
-pair of loop images have finite intersection. Retaining the individual
-recurrence shifts, spectral data, and effective Mignotte thresholds gives the
-cardinality bound in \Cref{thm:effective-slender-cfl-cardinality}, but not a
-closed bound in compact grammar-size parameters. This is a different global
-argument, not a strengthening of the weak MCFL pumping lemma.
+The affine recurrence action converts one synchronized pumping family into
+an injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Adic topology
+turns those returns into scatteredness and prime-support obstructions, while
+Evertse's quotient theorem and Schur's theorem identify the remaining
+bounded-support possibility as a geometric ray \(cb^t\). In standard
+weak-Perron greedy systems, the length squeeze classifies that possibility
+algebraically: it occurs if and only if a positive power of the weak Perron
+root is an integer.
 
-The Supplementary Information (Online Resource 1) contains the independent fixed-DFA density and
-regular Zeckendorf results. Keeping those comparisons outside the article
-leaves the main theorem chain centered on synchronized recurrence orbits
-and their arithmetic consequences.
+For slender context-free languages, a finite paired-loop cover supplies
+global control of every represented value. The same affine evaluation sends
+each loop to finitely many recurrence sequences, and dominant-root transfer
+followed by Mignotte's theorem gives the two-system Cobham finiteness result.
+Complete recurrence and loop data yield an effective cardinality bound. For
+the one-system geometric-ray problem, candidate verification is effective,
+but no uniform bound is known for the fan-out and block lengths of a smallest
+witness; this is the missing step toward a general decision procedure.

-\subsection{Relation to prior work}\label{subsec:prior-work}
+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a
+prefix beyond the recurrence transient, every digit acts by an integral
+matrix, and every block matrix is invertible modulo integers coprime to the
+trailing coefficient. The weak pumping lemma of
+Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami supplies one family in which finitely many
+fixed blocks are raised to a common exponent. A common order of their
+matrices in a finite general linear group gives the returns in Main
+Theorem A; positive pumped length and canonical uniqueness give
+distinctness.
 
-The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is classical, due to
-Hartmanis--Shank and Sch\"utzenberger
-\cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. Our language-theoretic input
-is exactly Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami's weak pumping lemma
-\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}: an infinite \(k\)-MCFL contains one family
-with \(2k\) fixed factors pumped by the same exponent. It says nothing
-about every sufficiently long word, and the corresponding strong pumping
-property fails for general MCFLs
-\cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}.
+These local returns place the orbit densely in the relevant congruence
+neighbourhoods. Broughan's adic classifications then yield the
+scattered-set obstruction. For nonunit recurrences, an intrinsic
+Cantor--Bendixson calculation after deleting the exceptional primes gives
+the alternative between new prime divisors and increasing exceptional
+valuations. In the unit case, the same returns also produce quotient
+congruences of arbitrary depth and a divisibility tree.
 
-Duncan--Elder--Frenkel--Lyu's newer substitution lemma
-\cite[Theorem~4.5]{DuncanElderFrenkelLiu2026} instead constrains every word
-with sufficiently many marked positions, but permits a switchable-tuple
-alternative to bounded pumping. Its substitutions are not a single
-one-parameter family of simultaneous powers of fixed blocks. They therefore
-do not give the fixed affine matrix powers, one return time for all
-parameters, or all-modulus return used here; nor do they replace the paired

+\subsection{Relation to prior work}
 
-The Supplementary Information (Online Resource 1) retains the finite-state results: the
-density dichotomy and effective fixed-DFA prime-slice bounds in ordinary
-bases, the corresponding Zeckendorf growth and regular-language results,

+The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is due to Hartmanis--Shank
+and Sch\"utzenberger \cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. Our
+language-theoretic input is the weak pumping lemma for MCFLs
+\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}, which supplies one synchronized family.
+The stronger pumping property fails for general MCFLs
+\cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}. The substitution lemma
+of Duncan--Elder--Frenkel--Lyu controls every sufficiently marked long word
+but allows switchable tuples rather than one fixed simultaneous-power
+orbit \cite[Theorem~4.5]{DuncanElderFrenkelLiu2026}; that distinction is
+why the older weak lemma gives the matrix powers used here.
 
+Evertse's quotient theorem is the arithmetic input for the geometric-ray
+step \cite[Theorem~3]{Evertse1984}; later \(S\)-part estimates concern the
+size of the supported part of recurrence terms
+\cite{BugeaudEvertse2017}. Broughan supplies the ambient adic
+classifications \cite{Broughan2003}. Frougny's normalization theorem and
+the Bertrand and substitution literature provide the regular canonical
+interfaces for Pisot numeration
+\cite{Frougny1992,BruyereHansel1997,Fabre1995,FrougnySolomyak1992}.
+Charlier--Kreczman obtain the residue-class quotient limits underlying the
+weak-Perron length squeeze \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025};
+the prime-support and MCFL classification is the additional interface
+proved here.
+
+For the two-system result, the paired-loop classification is due to
+Latteux--Thierrin and Ilie
+\cite{LatteuxThierrin1983,Ilie1994,IlieRozenbergSalomaa2000}, and the
+common-value input is Mignotte's theorem
+\cite{Mignotte1978Intersection}. Albayrak--Bell's quantitative
+Cobham--Semenov theorem contains the regular integer-base specialization
+and gives a stronger explicit automaton bound there
+\cite[Theorems~1.1 and 4.1]{AlbayrakBell2023}. Regular Perron-substitutive
+and regular abstract-numeration cases lie in existing Cobham theory
+\cite[Theorem~1]{Durand2011CobhamSubstitutions}%
+\cite[Theorem~49]{CharlierLeroyRigo2013CobhamANS}. The contribution of
+Main Theorem C is the passage from genuinely nonregular slender
+context-free representation languages to recurrence sequences in
+weak-Perron positional systems.

 \subsection{Organization}
 
-\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} begins with the context-free Zeckendorf
-motivation, develops the recurrent block action and synchronized MCFL orbit,
-proves the local-adic and prime-support consequences, establishes the
-geometric-ray characterization and its effective boundary, and concludes
-with the unit and weak-Perron specializations. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham}
-uses the global paired-loop classification to prove the separate two-system
-finiteness theorem, gives its effective cardinality refinement from complete
-presentations, and locates its nonregular contribution relative to existing
-Cobham results. \Cref{sec:conclusion} summarizes the proved scope and the
-remaining decision interface.
+\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} develops local rigidity from one synchronized
+orbit: the Zeckendorf model, affine recurrence action, prime-support
+obstructions, geometric-ray characterization, and weak-Perron
+classification. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham} develops global rigidity from a
+finite paired-loop cover and proves the two-system theorem and its effective
+cardinality refinement. Both branches use the passage
+\[
+  \text{structured word families}
+  \longrightarrow \text{affine matrix powers}
+  \longrightarrow \text{linear recurrences}
+  \longrightarrow \text{arithmetic rigidity}.

   \label{rem:general-decision-interface}
-  The preceding corollary does not yield a decision procedure. To turn

-  Positivity ask for signs of all or all sufficiently late terms; these
-  problems remain open in unrestricted order
-  \cite{OuaknineWorrell2012,AkshayBazilleGenestVahanwala2024}.

-  matrix equations include undecidable families
-  \cite{BellEtAl2008MatrixEquations}. Our candidate check instead asks

 \begin{abstract}
-Let \(U\) be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers that is
-eventually linearly recurrent, and suppose that a finite digit language
-gives unique representations. Combining the
-weak pumping lemma for multiple context-free languages with the affine
-recurrence action, we show that every infinite multiple context-free
-sublanguage contains one injective synchronized orbit returning
-modulo every integer coprime to the recurrence's trailing coefficient.
-Applying Broughan's standard adic classifications and our deleted-prime intrinsic
-Cantor--Bendixson calculation yields scattered-set obstructions, prime and
-bounded-\(\Omega\) MCF-immunity, and, in the unit case, quotient chains of
-arbitrary congruence depth and an induced countably branching divisibility
-tree.
-
-For the intrinsic minimal tail recurrence we prove an inverse theorem:
-bounded prime support away from its constant term occurs on an infinite
-MCFL if and only if the canonical language contains a synchronized ray
-whose values are \(cb^t\) with integers \(c\ge1\), \(b\ge2\). The
-arithmetic rigidity step is deduced explicitly from Evertse's theorem on
-prime ideals in quotients of nondegenerate recurrences. On the promised
-class of valid presentations, with a DFA and a supplied or effectively
-certified minimal tail recurrence, positive instances are semidecidable;
-the missing uniform witness bound for a general decision procedure is isolated. For
-standard greedy linear numeration bases whose minimal tail polynomial is
-the minimal polynomial of a weak Perron number \(\beta\), bounded support
-occurs exactly when some positive power of \(\beta\) is an integer. This
-includes regular alternating-radix systems with nonintegral
-\(\beta=\sqrt B\). The weak-pumping mechanism still extracts only one
-synchronized orbit; it gives neither global control of the canonical
-language nor simultaneous control in two numeration systems. Separately,
-the global paired-loop classification of slender context-free languages,
-combined with Mignotte's common-value theorem, proves that a set with
-slender context-free representations in two multiplicatively independent
-weak-Perron linear numeration systems is finite.
+Let \(U\) be a strictly increasing, eventually linearly recurrent sequence
+of positive place values with a finite canonical digit language. Every
+infinite multiple context-free sublanguage contains an injective
+synchronized orbit whose values return modulo each integer coprime to the
+trailing recurrence coefficient. These returns give prime-support and
+scatteredness obstructions, including MCF-immunity of the prime and
+bounded-\(\Omega\) representation languages. For the intrinsic minimal
+tail recurrence, bounded prime support occurs on an infinite
+multiple context-free sublanguage if and only if the canonical language
+contains a synchronized ray with values \(cb^t\), where \(c\ge1\) and
+\(b\ge2\). In a standard greedy system whose minimal tail polynomial is
+the minimal polynomial of a weak Perron number \(\beta\), this is equivalent
+to integrality of some positive power of \(\beta\). Finally, a finite
+paired-loop cover converts slender context-free representations into
+recurrence sequences: Mignotte's common-value theorem then implies that a
+set represented by slender context-free languages in two multiplicatively
+independent weak-Perron systems is finite. Complete effective presentations
+also yield a computable cardinality bound.

-\section{Conclusion and open interface}\label{sec:conclusion}
-
-The affine recurrence action turns one weak MCFL pumping family into a
-single injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Positive
-pumped length and uniqueness of canonical representation supply
-distinctness, while finite-group return times supply congruences. Applying
-Broughan's adic classifications to these orbits,
-together with the deleted-prime intrinsic derivative calculation, gives the
-scattered-set obstruction, the nonunit escape dichotomy, and prime and
-bounded-\(\Omega\) MCF-immunity.
-
-For the minimal tail recurrence, the residual bounded-support phenomenon
-has an exact structural form. It occurs on an infinite finite-fan-out MCFL
-if and only if the canonical language contains a synchronized ray with
-values \(cb^t\). Evertse's quotient theorem is used with an explicit
-prime-ideal norm bound to reduce a fixed-support recurrence to one
-characteristic root; Schur's theorem removes its polynomial factor. The
-ratio \(b\) uses only primes dividing the minimal tail constant. In a
-standard greedy linear numeration basis with weak-Perron recurrence, residue
-asymptotics and length thresholds show that such a ray exists exactly when
-some positive power of the weak Perron number is an integer. Alternating
-radices give an infinite family with nonintegral root \(\sqrt B\) and a
-regular ray of values \(B^t\).
-
-On the promised class of valid effectively presented regular canonical
-systems, with the minimal tail recurrence and threshold supplied or
-certified, positive promised instances can be enumerated and certified. The unresolved general step is not
-candidate verification but witness compression: no computable bound is
-known for the fan-out and word lengths of a smallest geometric synchronized
-scheme. DFA path compression does not preserve the associated affine
-recurrence matrices. Conversely, no reduction proving undecidability is
-known that also preserves unique canonical representation, the minimal tail
-recurrence, and the special digit-matrix form.
-Accordingly the general decision problem remains open, while the
-weak-Perron subclass has the exact algebraic classification above.
+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension
-problem for context-free sequences discussed by Caucal and Le Gonidec
-\cite{CaucalLeGonidec2014}; this paper does not settle it. The weak pumping
-mechanism itself still supplies only one ray inside one infinite MCFL, and
-two representations of the same set may supply unrelated rays with no
-common values. It neither controls every sufficiently long word nor the
-whole canonical language. The slender-context-free theorem proved here
-escapes that ceiling only because the Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie
-classification replaces a single pumped orbit by a finite paired-loop cover
-of each full representation language. Mignotte's theorem then makes every
-pair of loop images have finite intersection. Retaining the individual
-recurrence shifts, spectral data, and effective Mignotte thresholds gives the
-cardinality bound in \Cref{thm:effective-slender-cfl-cardinality}, but not a
-closed bound in compact grammar-size parameters. This is a different global
-argument, not a strengthening of the weak MCFL pumping lemma.
+The affine recurrence action converts one synchronized pumping family into
+an injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Adic topology
+turns those returns into scatteredness and prime-support obstructions, while
+Evertse's quotient theorem and Schur's theorem identify the remaining
+bounded-support possibility as a geometric ray \(cb^t\). In standard
+weak-Perron greedy systems, the length squeeze classifies that possibility
+algebraically: it occurs if and only if a positive power of the weak Perron
+root is an integer.
 
-The Supplementary Information (Online Resource 1) contains the independent fixed-DFA density and
-regular Zeckendorf results. Keeping those comparisons outside the article
-leaves the main theorem chain centered on synchronized recurrence orbits
-and their arithmetic consequences.
+For slender context-free languages, a finite paired-loop cover supplies
+global control of every represented value. The same affine evaluation sends
+each loop to finitely many recurrence sequences, and dominant-root transfer
+followed by Mignotte's theorem gives the two-system Cobham finiteness result.
+Complete recurrence and loop data yield an effective cardinality bound. For
+the one-system geometric-ray problem, candidate verification is effective,
+but no uniform bound is known for the fan-out and block lengths of a smallest
+witness; this is the missing step toward a general decision procedure.

+\begin{maintheorem}[C: slender context-free Cobham theorem]
+Let \(U\) and \(V\) be strictly increasing standard greedy linear
+numeration sequences whose minimal tail recurrence polynomials are the
+minimal polynomials of weak Perron numbers \(\alpha>1\) and \(\beta>1\).
+If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are multiplicatively independent and both
+\(\operatorname{Rep}_U(X)\) and \(\operatorname{Rep}_V(X)\) are slender

+\end{maintheorem}

+\subsection{Proof architecture}
 
-\subsection{Relation to prior work}\label{subsec:prior-work}
+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a
+prefix beyond the recurrence transient, every digit acts by an integral
+matrix, and every block matrix is invertible modulo integers coprime to the
+trailing coefficient. The weak pumping lemma of
+Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami supplies one family in which finitely many
+fixed blocks are raised to a common exponent. A common order of their
+matrices in a finite general linear group gives the returns in Main
+Theorem A; positive pumped length and canonical uniqueness give
+distinctness.
 
-The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is classical, due to
-Hartmanis--Shank and Sch\"utzenberger
-\cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. Our language-theoretic input
-is exactly Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami's weak pumping lemma
-\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}: an infinite \(k\)-MCFL contains one family
-with \(2k\) fixed factors pumped by the same exponent. It says nothing
-about every sufficiently long word, and the corresponding strong pumping
-property fails for general MCFLs
-\cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}.
+These local returns place the orbit densely in the relevant congruence
+neighbourhoods. Broughan's adic classifications then yield the
+scattered-set obstruction. For nonunit recurrences, an intrinsic
+Cantor--Bendixson calculation after deleting the exceptional primes gives
+the alternative between new prime divisors and increasing exceptional
+valuations. In the unit case, the same returns also produce quotient
+congruences of arbitrary depth and a divisibility tree.
 
-Duncan--Elder--Frenkel--Lyu's newer substitution lemma
-\cite[Theorem~4.5]{DuncanElderFrenkelLiu2026} instead constrains every word
-with sufficiently many marked positions, but permits a switchable-tuple
-alternative to bounded pumping. Its substitutions are not a single
-one-parameter family of simultaneous powers of fixed blocks. They therefore
-do not give the fixed affine matrix powers, one return time for all
-parameters, or all-modulus return used here; nor do they replace the paired
-Ogden pump in the Zeckendorf argument. No immunity conclusion of this paper
-follows directly from that lemma. We use the older weak lemma because it
-provides exactly one fixed synchronized orbit. Placing that orbit beyond the
-recurrence transient, proving its finite-group returns, and deriving the
-prime-support consequences are the contributions here.
+For Main Theorem B, a bounded-support orbit is restricted to an arithmetic
+subsequence supported on a fixed finite set of primes. Its values form a
+pairwise distinct positive linear recurrence. Evertse's theorem on prime
+ideals in quotients excludes two or more characteristic roots after the
+root-of-unity classes are separated; Schur's theorem excludes a
+nonconstant polynomial factor. A further arithmetic subsequence therefore
+has values \(cb^t\). The converse is supplied by an explicit linear MCFG
+for every synchronized ray.

-The Supplementary Information (Online Resource 1) retains the finite-state results: the

+The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is due to Hartmanis--Shank
+and Sch\"utzenberger \cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. Our
+language-theoretic input is the weak pumping lemma for MCFLs
+\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}, which supplies one synchronized family.
+The stronger pumping property fails for general MCFLs
+\cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}. The substitution lemma
+of Duncan--Elder--Frenkel--Lyu controls every sufficiently marked long word
+but allows switchable tuples rather than one fixed simultaneous-power
+orbit \cite[Theorem~4.5]{DuncanElderFrenkelLiu2026}; that distinction is
+why the older weak lemma gives the matrix powers used here.
 
+Evertse's quotient theorem is the arithmetic input for the geometric-ray
+step \cite[Theorem~3]{Evertse1984}; later \(S\)-part estimates concern the
+size of the supported part of recurrence terms
+\cite{BugeaudEvertse2017}. Broughan supplies the ambient adic
+classifications \cite{Broughan2003}. Frougny's normalization theorem and
+the Bertrand and substitution literature provide the regular canonical
+interfaces for Pisot numeration
+\cite{Frougny1992,BruyereHansel1997,Fabre1995,FrougnySolomyak1992}.
+Charlier--Kreczman obtain the residue-class quotient limits underlying the
+weak-Perron length squeeze \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025};
+the prime-support and MCFL classification is the additional interface
+proved here.
+
+For the two-system result, the paired-loop classification is due to
+Latteux--Thierrin and Ilie
+\cite{LatteuxThierrin1983,Ilie1994,IlieRozenbergSalomaa2000}, and the
+common-value input is Mignotte's theorem
+\cite{Mignotte1978Intersection}. Albayrak--Bell's quantitative
+Cobham--Semenov theorem contains the regular integer-base specialization
+and gives a stronger explicit automaton bound there
+\cite[Theorems~1.1 and 4.1]{AlbayrakBell2023}. Regular Perron-substitutive
+and regular abstract-numeration cases lie in existing Cobham theory
+\cite[Theorem~1]{Durand2011CobhamSubstitutions}%
+\cite[Theorem~49]{CharlierLeroyRigo2013CobhamANS}. The contribution of
+Main Theorem C is the passage from genuinely nonregular slender
+context-free representation languages to recurrence sequences in
+weak-Perron positional systems.

-\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} begins with the context-free Zeckendorf

+cardinality refinement. Both branches use the passage

\begin{theorem}[Arbitrarily deep quotient congruences]
  \label{thm:unit-mcfl-deep-congruence-chain}
  Suppose \(\abs{a_0}=1\), and let \(L\subseteq\mathcal R_U\) be an
  infinite MCFL. For arbitrary sequences \(M_i\ge1\) and \(r_i\ge1\),
  \(L\) contains a strictly increasing sequence \(N_i\) such that
  \[
    N_{i+1}=N_iQ_i,\qquad Q_i>1,\qquad
    Q_i\equiv1\pmod {M_iN_i^{r_i}}.
  \]
  If \(M_i\) is divisible by every prime at most \(B_i\), then every
  prime divisor of \(Q_i\) exceeds \(B_i\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
  Take the fixed orbit \(N(t)\) from
  \Cref{thm:mcfl-synchronized-congruence-orbit}, discarding finitely many
  initial parameters so that \(N(t)\ge2\). Having selected
  \(N_i=N(t_i)\), apply the synchronized congruence with
  \[
    q_i=M_iN_i^{r_i+1}.
  \]
  The values \(N(t_i+mH(q_i))\), \(m\ge1\), are pairwise distinct and all
  are congruent to \(N_i\) modulo \(q_i\). Only finitely many positive
  integers are at most \(N_i\), so choose \(m_i\ge1\) for which
  \(N(t_i+m_iH(q_i))>N_i\), and set
  \(t_{i+1}=t_i+m_iH(q_i)\). The congruence gives
  \[
    N_{i+1}=N_i+c_iM_iN_i^{r_i+1}
           =N_i(1+c_iM_iN_i^{r_i})
  \]
  for an integer \(c_i\ge1\). This proves the first assertion. Under
  the last hypothesis, \(Q_i\equiv1\pmod p\) for every prime
  \(p\le B_i\), so none of those primes divides \(Q_i\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Induced full divisibility tree]
  \label{thm:unit-mcfl-divisibility-tree}
  Under the hypotheses of
  \Cref{thm:unit-mcfl-deep-congruence-chain}, there is an injection
  \[
    \Phi:\NN^{<\omega}\longrightarrow L
  \]
  such that
  \[
    \val_U(\Phi(\sigma))\mid\val_U(\Phi(\tau))
      \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sigma\preceq\tau,
  \]
  where \(\preceq\) denotes the prefix order. The quotients attached to
  distinct edges can be chosen pairwise coprime. Moreover, given an
  arbitrary prescribed threshold for each edge, every prime divisor of
  its quotient can be required to exceed that threshold.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
  Use the fixed pairwise-distinct orbit from
  \Cref{thm:mcfl-synchronized-congruence-orbit}. Here is an explicit
  parent-before-child enumeration. If \(p_i\) is the \(i\)-th prime, encode
  \(\sigma=(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_{m-1})\) by
  \[
    \kappa(\sigma)=2^m\prod_{i=0}^{m-1}p_{i+2}^{\sigma_i+1}.
  \]
  Unique factorization makes \(\kappa\) injective, and
  \(\kappa(\sigma^\frown j)>\kappa(\sigma)\). Enumerating the nonroot
  nodes, equivalently their incoming edges, by increasing \(\kappa\)
  therefore has order type \(\omega\) and places every parent before each
  child. Map
  the root to any orbit word of value \(R_0\ge2\). Suppose finitely many
  edges have been assigned, and consider a new edge from a parent of
  value \(P\). Let \(R\) be divisible by \(R_0\), by every previously
  assigned edge quotient, and by every prime not exceeding the prescribed
  threshold for the new edge. Apply the synchronized orbit congruence
  modulo \(P^2R\) at the parameter of the parent. Positive multiples of
  the return time give pairwise distinct positive values in the indicated
  congruence class. Only finitely many are at most \(P\), so some multiple
  gives an unused orbit word of value \(P'>P\) with
  \[
    P'\equiv P\pmod {P^2R}.
  \]
  Hence \(P'=PQ\), where \(Q>1\) and \(Q\equiv1\pmod {PR}\). In
  particular, \(Q\) is coprime to the root and to every earlier edge
  quotient, and no prime up to the prescribed threshold divides \(Q\).

  Recursion defines \(\Phi\) on every node. The value at a node is the
  root value times the product of the edge quotients along its path.
  Since the root and all distinct edge quotients are pairwise coprime,
  the value at \(\sigma\) divides the value at \(\tau\) exactly when the
  root-to-\(\sigma\) edge set is contained in the root-to-\(\tau\) edge
  set. For two nodes of a rooted tree, containment of their root-path edge
  sets holds exactly when the first node is an ancestor of the second;
  here this is precisely \(\sigma\preceq\tau\). This also proves injectivity.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Consequences for standard greedy systems}

\begin{corollary}
  \label{thm:recurrent-numeration-prime-cf-immunity}
  Let \((U,A,\mathcal R_U)\) satisfy \textup{(U1)}, \textup{(U2)}, and
  \textup{(U3)}, and put
  \[
    \mathcal P_U
      :=\{w\in\mathcal R_U:\val_U(w)\text{ is prime}\}.
  \]
  Then \(\mathcal P_U\) is MCF-immune, and therefore CF-immune,
  REG-immune, and not recognizable by a finite automaton over \(A\).

  If, in addition, \(\abs{a_0}=1\), then every infinite multiple
  context-free
  \(L\subseteq\mathcal R_U\) has unbounded
  \(\omega(\val_U(w))\). More precisely, \(L\) contains a
  coprime-quotient chain \(N_{i+1}=N_iQ_i\) with
  \(Q_i>1\) and \(Q_i\equiv1\pmod {N_i}\). Thus the bounded-\(\omega\),
  bounded-\(\Omega\), and finite-prime-support languages of a unit
  system are MCF-immune whenever they are infinite. Without the unit
  hypothesis, every bounded-\(\Omega\) language is still MCF-immune.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
  The MCF-immunity assertions follow from
  \Cref{thm:nonunit-mcfl-escape-dichotomy}, including its
  bounded-\(\Omega\) conclusion. In a unit system \(S\) is empty, so
  that theorem gives unbounded \(\omega\). Taking
  \(M_i=r_i=1\) in
  \Cref{thm:unit-mcfl-deep-congruence-chain} gives the stated chain.
  Regular languages are context-free and context-free languages are
  MCFLs. Finally, \textup{(U2)} and Euclid's theorem make
  \(\mathcal P_U\) infinite.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Greedy length interval.}
For a standard greedy linear numeration basis with \(U_0=1\), a positive
integer has a canonical greedy word of length \(m\) if and only if it lies
in the half-open interval
\[
  [U_{m-1},U_m).
\]
Indeed, the greedy algorithm chooses the least threshold \(U_m\) strictly
larger than the represented integer; minimality of \(m\) gives the lower
bound, and the choice of \(U_m\) gives the upper bound. This is a property
of the standard greedy subclass, not an assumption on the ambient
canonical eventually recurrent systems.

\begin{corollary}
  \label{cor:linear-perron-prime-cf-immunity}
  Let \(U=(U_n)_{n\ge0}\) be a standard greedy linear numeration basis in
  the following precise sense: \(U_0=1\), the \(U_n\) are strictly
  increasing integers with bounded quotients, \(\mathcal R_U\) is the LSD-first
  reversal of the usual greedy representation language, and \(U\)
  has minimal tail recurrence polynomial equal to the minimal polynomial
  of a Perron number \(\beta\). Thus
  \(\beta>1\) is a real algebraic integer and every other conjugate
  \(\beta'\) satisfies \(\abs{\beta'}<\beta\); compare
  \cite{LindMarcus1995,Rigo2014Vol2}. Then its prime
  representation language is MCF-immune, hence CF-immune, REG-immune and
  nonrecognizable. The same statements hold in the usual MSD-first
  convention.

  If the dominant Perron number is a unit and the chosen recurrence has
  trailing coefficient \(a_0=\pm1\), then the full coprime-quotient and
  bounded-prime-support MCF-immunity conclusions of
  \Cref{thm:recurrent-numeration-prime-cf-immunity} hold.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
  Greedy expansion gives a unique representation of every positive
  integer, and its length-\(m\) words represent values between successive
  place-value thresholds; thus \textup{(U1)} and \textup{(U2)} hold. The defining
  Perron recurrence gives \textup{(U3)}. Apply
  \Cref{thm:recurrent-numeration-prime-cf-immunity}. The immunity proof
  uses only \textup{(U1)}, \textup{(U2)}, and \textup{(U3)} and does not
  assume that the full greedy language is regular. In the Pisot subclass,
  Frougny's finite
  normalization theorem supplies a finite transducer, and the associated
  canonical syntax and Bertrand/substitution descriptions are standard
  \cite{Frougny1992,BruyereHansel1997,Fabre1995,FrougnySolomyak1992}.
  Finally, multiple context-free, context-free, and
  regular languages are closed under reversal, so changing between the LSD-first proof
  convention and the usual MSD-first convention preserves every
  conclusion.
\end{proof}

  Tribonacci recurrence has \(X^3-X^2-X-1\). Their trailing recurrence

+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a
+prefix beyond the recurrence transient, every digit acts by an integral
+matrix, and every block matrix is invertible modulo integers coprime to the
+trailing coefficient. The weak pumping lemma of

+fixed blocks are raised to a common exponent. A common order of their

+distinctness.

 \subsection{Organization}
 
-\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} begins with the context-free Zeckendorf
-motivation, develops the recurrent block action and synchronized MCFL orbit,
-proves the local-adic and prime-support consequences, establishes the
-geometric-ray characterization and its effective boundary, and concludes
-with the unit and weak-Perron specializations. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham}
-uses the global paired-loop classification to prove the separate two-system
-finiteness theorem, gives its effective cardinality refinement from complete
-presentations, and locates its nonregular contribution relative to existing
-Cobham results. \Cref{sec:conclusion} summarizes the proved scope and the
-remaining decision interface.
+\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} develops local rigidity from one synchronized
+orbit: the Zeckendorf model, affine recurrence action, prime-support
+obstructions, geometric-ray characterization, and weak-Perron
+classification. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham} develops global rigidity from a
+finite paired-loop cover and proves the two-system theorem and its effective
+cardinality refinement. Both branches use the passage
+\[
+  \text{structured word families}
+  \longrightarrow \text{affine matrix powers}
+  \longrightarrow \text{linear recurrences}
+  \longrightarrow \text{arithmetic rigidity}.
+\]

+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension

+\begin{maintheorem}[C: slender context-free Cobham theorem]

+If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are multiplicatively independent and both
+\(\operatorname{Rep}_U(X)\) and \(\operatorname{Rep}_V(X)\) are slender
+context-free languages, then \(X\) is finite.
+\end{maintheorem}
 
-There are two resolved regimes. When the trailing coefficient is a unit,
-the synchronized orbit admits quotient congruences of arbitrary prescribed

-pairwise coprime, arbitrarily rough edge quotients

-geometric-ray properties above hold exactly when some positive power of the
-weak Perron number is an integer
-(\Cref{cor:linear-perron-bounded-support-classification}). Hence the

-imprimitive examples such as alternating-radix systems with
-\(\beta=\sqrt B\) give genuinely nonintegral positive cases. The

-Charlier--Kreczman obtain residue-class quotient limits for regular
-positional systems and record the corresponding converse for eventually
-increasing linear recurrences whose dominating eigenvalues have a common
-power \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025}. Our
-contribution here is the prime-support/MCFL interface and its exact
-geometric-ray and algebraic classification, not that quotient-limit
-mechanism.
+This is \Cref{thm:slender-cfl-cobham}. With complete recurrence and
+paired-loop data, \Cref{thm:effective-slender-cfl-cardinality} gives a

-A separate two-system result begins from a different language-theoretic
-input. The Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie classification gives a finite paired-loop
-cover of an entire slender context-free language. Combining that global
-cover with the affine block action, the weak-Perron residue asymptotics, and
-Mignotte's common-value theorem for recurrence sequences yields

-sets \cite[Theorems~1.1 and 4.1]{AlbayrakBell2023}. It contains the regular
-integer-base specialization, covers regular sparse (in particular regular
-poly-slender) tuple languages more broadly, and supplies an explicit
-automaton-data bound. Regular Perron-substitutive and regular abstract-

-\cite[Theorem~1]{Durand2011CobhamSubstitutions}%

-weak-Perron positional systems. This is not an extension of the one-orbit
-pumping theorem: it does not use finite-group returns, deleted-prime
-topology, fixed-support quotient rigidity, geometric subsequences, or the

-\subsection{Relation to prior work}\label{subsec:prior-work}
+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a
+prefix beyond the recurrence transient, every digit acts by an integral
+matrix, and every block matrix is invertible modulo integers coprime to the
+trailing coefficient. The weak pumping lemma of
+Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami supplies one family in which finitely many
+fixed blocks are raised to a common exponent. A common order of their
+matrices in a finite general linear group gives the returns in Main
+Theorem A; positive pumped length and canonical uniqueness give
+distinctness.
 
-The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is classical, due to
-Hartmanis--Shank and Sch\"utzenberger
-\cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. Our language-theoretic input
-is exactly Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami's weak pumping lemma
-\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}: an infinite \(k\)-MCFL contains one family
-with \(2k\) fixed factors pumped by the same exponent. It says nothing
-about every sufficiently long word, and the corresponding strong pumping
-property fails for general MCFLs
-\cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}.
+These local returns place the orbit densely in the relevant congruence
+neighbourhoods. Broughan's adic classifications then yield the
+scattered-set obstruction. For nonunit recurrences, an intrinsic
+Cantor--Bendixson calculation after deleting the exceptional primes gives
+the alternative between new prime divisors and increasing exceptional
+valuations. In the unit case, the same returns also produce quotient
+congruences of arbitrary depth and a divisibility tree.
 
-Duncan--Elder--Frenkel--Lyu's newer substitution lemma
-\cite[Theorem~4.5]{DuncanElderFrenkelLiu2026} instead constrains every word
-with sufficiently many marked positions, but permits a switchable-tuple
-alternative to bounded pumping. Its substitutions are not a single
-one-parameter family of simultaneous powers of fixed blocks. They therefore
-do not give the fixed affine matrix powers, one return time for all
-parameters, or all-modulus return used here; nor do they replace the paired
-Ogden pump in the Zeckendorf argument. No immunity conclusion of this paper
-follows directly from that lemma. We use the older weak lemma because it
-provides exactly one fixed synchronized orbit. Placing that orbit beyond the
-recurrence transient, proving its finite-group returns, and deriving the
-prime-support consequences are the contributions here.
+For Main Theorem B, a bounded-support orbit is restricted to an arithmetic
+subsequence supported on a fixed finite set of primes. Its values form a
+pairwise distinct positive linear recurrence. Evertse's theorem on prime
+ideals in quotients excludes two or more characteristic roots after the
+root-of-unity classes are separated; Schur's theorem excludes a
+nonconstant polynomial factor. A further arithmetic subsequence therefore
+has values \(cb^t\). The converse is supplied by an explicit linear MCFG
+for every synchronized ray.
 
-Evertse's theorem on sums of \(S\)-units and linear recurrences is the
-nearest arithmetic input \cite{Evertse1984}. It supplies exactly the
-unbounded prime-ideal support in term quotients needed for the geometric
-rigidity step; it does not state the synchronized-language characterization.
-Later \(S\)-part estimates for recurrence terms, such as

-deleted-prime sets and their intrinsic derivative, and the resulting

-Frougny's
-normalization theorem and the Bertrand and substitution literature provide
-the regular canonical interfaces for Pisot numeration
-\cite{Frougny1992,BruyereHansel1997,Fabre1995,FrougnySolomyak1992}.
+In a weak-Perron greedy system, peripheral conjugates become equal after a
+common power. Residue-class asymptotics and the greedy length interval
+squeeze the geometric ratio to \(b=\beta^D\), where \(D\) is the total
+pumped length. This proves the algebraic classification in Main Theorem B
+without assuming that the full greedy language is regular.
 
-Charlier--Kreczman remove the dominant-root restriction from the regularity
-problem for positional numeration systems \cite{CharlierKreczman2025}.
-They associate a periodic alternate real base to the residue classes of the
-place-value sequence and give a full characterization of regularity through
-the graph of the greedy and quasi-greedy expansions of (1) in the shifted
-alternate bases. Their procedure is a semidecision in general, and becomes a
-decision procedure when the associated alternate base is known to be Parry.
-Their Proposition~10 proves that regularity of the whole greedy language
-forces residue-class consecutive-quotient limits. More directly relevant
-here, Remark~12 states that, for an arbitrary linear recurrence, equality of
-the (p)-th powers of its dominating eigenvalues implies convergence of
-\(U_n/U_{n-p}\) to that common power when \((\lvert U_n\rvert)\) is
-eventually increasing. Under the irreducible weak-Perron hypotheses below,
-separability gives equal peripheral multiplicities, weak-Perron periodicity
-gives the common power, and strict increase supplies their last hypothesis.
-Thus their work already contains the root-growth mechanism needed for our
-length squeeze, in essentially equivalent quotient-limit form. We retain a
-self-contained coefficient-level proof because it identifies every residue
-coefficient and verifies positivity under exactly our hypotheses. Their

-MCFL sublanguages, bounded prime support, synchronized geometric schemes, or
-the five equivalent conditions proved here; conversely, our theorem does not
-characterize regularity of the whole greedy language.
+Slenderness provides global rather than local control: the

 \subsection{Organization}
 
-\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} begins with the context-free Zeckendorf
-motivation, develops the recurrent block action and synchronized MCFL orbit,
-proves the local-adic and prime-support consequences, establishes the
-geometric-ray characterization and its effective boundary, and concludes
-with the unit and weak-Perron specializations. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham}
-uses the global paired-loop classification to prove the separate two-system
-finiteness theorem, gives its effective cardinality refinement from complete
-presentations, and locates its nonregular contribution relative to existing
-Cobham results. \Cref{sec:conclusion} summarizes the proved scope and the
-remaining decision interface.
+\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} develops local rigidity from one synchronized
+orbit: the Zeckendorf model, affine recurrence action, prime-support
+obstructions, geometric-ray characterization, and weak-Perron
+classification. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham} develops global rigidity from a
+finite paired-loop cover and proves the two-system theorem and its effective
+cardinality refinement. Both branches use the passage
+\[
+  \text{structured word families}
+  \longrightarrow \text{affine matrix powers}
+  \longrightarrow \text{linear recurrences}
+  \longrightarrow \text{arithmetic rigidity}.
+\]

-  constant and pumped-block length at most \(B\). No such compression

-  Positivity ask for signs of all or all sufficiently late terms; these
-  problems remain open in unrestricted order

-  intersection \cite{TarasovVyalyi2011}, while unrestricted multiplicative
-  matrix equations include undecidable families
-  \cite{BellEtAl2008MatrixEquations}. Our candidate check instead asks
-  whether the explicitly constructed recurrence
-  \(N(t+1)-bN(t)\) is identically zero; no reduction in either direction is
-  claimed. None of these observations is a reduction for the companion-form
-  digit matrices here, and conditions

-  weak-Perron subclass of greedy linear numeration bases is resolved

+  A decision procedure would follow from a computable bound \(B\), derived
+  from the input DFA and minimal tail recurrence, such that every positive
+  instance has a geometric synchronized scheme whose fan-out and total
+  block length are at most \(B\). No such bound is known. Replacing a long

+  recurrence matrix and destroy the identity
+  \(\val_U(W(t+1))=b\val_U(W(t))\). The positive semidecision therefore

517: \begin{example}[Pisot and non-Pisot Perron systems]
518:   \label{ex:pisot-unit-nonunit}
519:   The Fibonacci recurrence has characteristic polynomial
520:   \(X^2-X-1\), the Pell recurrence has \(X^2-2X-1\), and the
521:   Tribonacci recurrence has \(X^3-X^2-X-1\). Their trailing recurrence
522:   coefficient is \(a_0=1\), so the iterated conclusion applies. In
523:   ordinary base \(b\), \(U_n=b^n\) and \(a_0=b\); prime MCF-immunity
524:   follows, strengthening the classical fixed-base CF-immunity conclusion
525:   to MCF-immunity, but the unit iteration is not being asserted.
526: 
527:   There is also an infinite family of genuinely nonintegral weak-Perron
528:   systems. Let \(p,q\ge2\), put \(B=pq\), and suppose that \(B\) is not a
529:   square. Define
530:   \[
531:     U_{2t}=B^t,\qquad U_{2t+1}=pB^t\qquad(t\ge0).
532:   \]
533:   The successive quotients are alternately \(p\) and \(q\). Repeated
534:   Euclidean division in these alternating radices gives every positive
535:   integer a unique greedy expansion: the digit at an even position lies
536:   in \(\{0,\ldots,p-1\}\), and the digit at an odd position lies in
537:   \(\{0,\ldots,q-1\}\). Hence the LSD-first canonical language is regular,
538:   since a finite automaton need only track position parity, the relevant
539:   digit bound, and a nonzero final digit. Moreover,
540:   \[
541:     U_{n+2}=BU_n,
542:   \]
543:   and the irreducible polynomial \(X^2-B\) is the minimal recurrence
544:   polynomial. Its positive root \(\sqrt B\) is nonintegral and weak Perron,
545:   with conjugate \(-\sqrt B\) of the same modulus. The regular ray
546:   \(\{0^{2t}1:t\ge0\}\) has values \(B^t\). Thus \(p=2,q=3\) gives the
547:   sequence \(1,2,6,12,36,72,\ldots\), while \(p=2,q=5\) gives a second
548:   concrete member \(1,2,10,20,100,200,\ldots\).
549: 
550:   A genuinely nonintegral, nonunit Pisot example is obtained from
551:   \[

553:     U_{n+2}=2U_{n+1}+2U_n.
554:   \]

556:   \[
557:     \frac{U_{n+2}}{U_{n+1}}
558:       =2+\frac{2U_n}{U_{n+1}}\in[8/3,3),
559:   \]
560:   so induction from \(U_1/U_0=3\) proves strict increase and bounded
561:   quotients. The irreducible polynomial \(X^2-2X-2\) annihilates this
562:   nonzero rational sequence, hence is its minimal tail polynomial. Its
563:   dominant root is \(1+\sqrt3\), and its trailing coefficient is
564:   \(a_0=2\), so the action is singular modulo \(2\). Nevertheless,
565:   \Cref{cor:linear-perron-bounded-support-classification} shows that every
566:   infinite MCFL in this nonintegral system acquires unbounded prime support
567:   away from \(2\); singularity of the ambient action does not produce a
568:   valuation-only escape language.
569: 
570:   The polynomial \(X^2-5X+5\) gives a genuinely non-Pisot instance. Its
571:   dominant root \(\beta=(5+\sqrt5)/2\) is Perron, while its other conjugate
572:   \((5-\sqrt5)/2\) is greater than one. The integer sequence
573:   \[

578:   \[

-\subsection{Relation to prior work}\label{subsec:prior-work}
+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a
+prefix beyond the recurrence transient, every digit acts by an integral
+matrix, and every block matrix is invertible modulo integers coprime to the
+trailing coefficient. The weak pumping lemma of
+Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami supplies one family in which finitely many
+fixed blocks are raised to a common exponent. A common order of their
+matrices in a finite general linear group gives the returns in Main
+Theorem A; positive pumped length and canonical uniqueness give
+distinctness.
 
-The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is classical, due to
-Hartmanis--Shank and Sch\"utzenberger
-\cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. Our language-theoretic input
-is exactly Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami's weak pumping lemma
-\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}: an infinite \(k\)-MCFL contains one family
-with \(2k\) fixed factors pumped by the same exponent. It says nothing
-about every sufficiently long word, and the corresponding strong pumping
-property fails for general MCFLs

+These local returns place the orbit densely in the relevant congruence
+neighbourhoods. Broughan's adic classifications then yield the

+Cantor--Bendixson calculation after deleting the exceptional primes gives
+the alternative between new prime divisors and increasing exceptional
+valuations. In the unit case, the same returns also produce quotient
+congruences of arbitrary depth and a divisibility tree.

 \subsection{Organization}
 
-\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} begins with the context-free Zeckendorf
-motivation, develops the recurrent block action and synchronized MCFL orbit,
-proves the local-adic and prime-support consequences, establishes the
-geometric-ray characterization and its effective boundary, and concludes
-with the unit and weak-Perron specializations. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham}
-uses the global paired-loop classification to prove the separate two-system
-finiteness theorem, gives its effective cardinality refinement from complete
-presentations, and locates its nonregular contribution relative to existing
-Cobham results. \Cref{sec:conclusion} summarizes the proved scope and the
-remaining decision interface.
+\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} develops local rigidity from one synchronized
+orbit: the Zeckendorf model, affine recurrence action, prime-support
+obstructions, geometric-ray characterization, and weak-Perron
+classification. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham} develops global rigidity from a
+finite paired-loop cover and proves the two-system theorem and its effective
+cardinality refinement. Both branches use the passage
+\[
+  \text{structured word families}
+  \longrightarrow \text{affine matrix powers}
+  \longrightarrow \text{linear recurrences}
+  \longrightarrow \text{arithmetic rigidity}.
+\]

+\begin{remark}[Decision boundary]
   \label{rem:general-decision-interface}
-  The preceding corollary does not yield a decision procedure. To turn
-  its enumeration into one, it would suffice to compute from the input
-  DFA and minimal tail recurrence a bound \(B\) such that every positive
-  instance has a geometric synchronized scheme with fan-out and total
-  constant and pumped-block length at most \(B\). No such compression
-  follows from DFA pumping: replacing a long loop by a shorter word with
-  the same DFA endpoints need not preserve its affine recurrence matrix,
-  and can therefore destroy the identity
-  \(\val_U(W(t+1))=b\val_U(W(t))\).
-
-  The neighboring decision theory does not close this step. Skolem asks
-  whether one term of a recurrence vanishes, while Positivity and Ultimate
-  Positivity ask for signs of all or all sufficiently late terms; these
-  problems remain open in unrestricted order
-  \cite{OuaknineWorrell2012,AkshayBazilleGenestVahanwala2024}.
-  Tarasov--Vyalyi relate an orbit-hitting problem to regular-language
-  intersection \cite{TarasovVyalyi2011}, while unrestricted multiplicative
-  matrix equations include undecidable families
-  \cite{BellEtAl2008MatrixEquations}. Our candidate check instead asks
-  whether the explicitly constructed recurrence

-  claimed. None of these observations is a reduction for the companion-form
-  digit matrices here, and conditions

-  effective statement is exactly the positive semidecision above. The
-  weak-Perron subclass of greedy linear numeration bases is resolved

+  A decision procedure would follow from a computable bound \(B\), derived
+  from the input DFA and minimal tail recurrence, such that every positive
+  instance has a geometric synchronized scheme whose fan-out and total
+  block length are at most \(B\). No such bound is known. Replacing a long

+  recurrence matrix and destroy the identity
+  \(\val_U(W(t+1))=b\val_U(W(t))\). The positive semidecision therefore

+\begin{maintheorem}[C: slender context-free Cobham theorem]

-\subsection{Relation to prior work}\label{subsec:prior-work}
+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a
+prefix beyond the recurrence transient, every digit acts by an integral
+matrix, and every block matrix is invertible modulo integers coprime to the
+trailing coefficient. The weak pumping lemma of
+Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami supplies one family in which finitely many
+fixed blocks are raised to a common exponent. A common order of their
+matrices in a finite general linear group gives the returns in Main
+Theorem A; positive pumped length and canonical uniqueness give
+distinctness.
 
-The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is classical, due to
-Hartmanis--Shank and Sch\"utzenberger
-\cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. Our language-theoretic input
-is exactly Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami's weak pumping lemma
-\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}: an infinite \(k\)-MCFL contains one family
-with \(2k\) fixed factors pumped by the same exponent. It says nothing
-about every sufficiently long word, and the corresponding strong pumping
-property fails for general MCFLs

+These local returns place the orbit densely in the relevant congruence
+neighbourhoods. Broughan's adic classifications then yield the

+Cantor--Bendixson calculation after deleting the exceptional primes gives
+the alternative between new prime divisors and increasing exceptional
+valuations. In the unit case, the same returns also produce quotient
+congruences of arbitrary depth and a divisibility tree.

-prime-support consequences are the contributions here.

+subsequence supported on a fixed finite set of primes. Its values form a

 \subsection{Organization}
 
-\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} begins with the context-free Zeckendorf
-motivation, develops the recurrent block action and synchronized MCFL orbit,
-proves the local-adic and prime-support consequences, establishes the
-geometric-ray characterization and its effective boundary, and concludes
-with the unit and weak-Perron specializations. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham}
-uses the global paired-loop classification to prove the separate two-system
-finiteness theorem, gives its effective cardinality refinement from complete
-presentations, and locates its nonregular contribution relative to existing
-Cobham results. \Cref{sec:conclusion} summarizes the proved scope and the
-remaining decision interface.
+\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} develops local rigidity from one synchronized
+orbit: the Zeckendorf model, affine recurrence action, prime-support
+obstructions, geometric-ray characterization, and weak-Perron
+classification. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham} develops global rigidity from a
+finite paired-loop cover and proves the two-system theorem and its effective
+cardinality refinement. Both branches use the passage
+\[
+  \text{structured word families}
+  \longrightarrow \text{affine matrix powers}
+  \longrightarrow \text{linear recurrences}
+  \longrightarrow \text{arithmetic rigidity}.
+\]

+\begin{remark}[Decision boundary]
   \label{rem:general-decision-interface}
-  The preceding corollary does not yield a decision procedure. To turn
-  its enumeration into one, it would suffice to compute from the input
-  DFA and minimal tail recurrence a bound \(B\) such that every positive
-  instance has a geometric synchronized scheme with fan-out and total
-  constant and pumped-block length at most \(B\). No such compression
-  follows from DFA pumping: replacing a long loop by a shorter word with
-  the same DFA endpoints need not preserve its affine recurrence matrix,
-  and can therefore destroy the identity
-  \(\val_U(W(t+1))=b\val_U(W(t))\).
-
-  The neighboring decision theory does not close this step. Skolem asks
-  whether one term of a recurrence vanishes, while Positivity and Ultimate
-  Positivity ask for signs of all or all sufficiently late terms; these
-  problems remain open in unrestricted order
-  \cite{OuaknineWorrell2012,AkshayBazilleGenestVahanwala2024}.
-  Tarasov--Vyalyi relate an orbit-hitting problem to regular-language
-  intersection \cite{TarasovVyalyi2011}, while unrestricted multiplicative
-  matrix equations include undecidable families
-  \cite{BellEtAl2008MatrixEquations}. Our candidate check instead asks
-  whether the explicitly constructed recurrence
-  \(N(t+1)-bN(t)\) is identically zero; no reduction in either direction is
-  claimed. None of these observations is a reduction for the companion-form
-  digit matrices here, and conditions
-  \textup{(U1)}, \textup{(U2)}, and \textup{(U4)} must also be preserved.
-  Thus general decidability,

-  effective statement is exactly the positive semidecision above. The
-  weak-Perron subclass of greedy linear numeration bases is resolved

+  A decision procedure would follow from a computable bound \(B\), derived
+  from the input DFA and minimal tail recurrence, such that every positive
+  instance has a geometric synchronized scheme whose fan-out and total
+  block length are at most \(B\). No such bound is known. Replacing a long
+  DFA loop by a shorter word with the same endpoints can change its affine
+  recurrence matrix and destroy the identity
+  \(\val_U(W(t+1))=b\val_U(W(t))\). The positive semidecision therefore
+  establishes neither decidability nor undecidability of the general

+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension
-problem for context-free sequences discussed by Caucal and Le Gonidec
-\cite{CaucalLeGonidec2014}; this paper does not settle it. The weak pumping
-mechanism itself still supplies only one ray inside one infinite MCFL, and
-two representations of the same set may supply unrelated rays with no
-common values. It neither controls every sufficiently long word nor the
-whole canonical language. The slender-context-free theorem proved here
-escapes that ceiling only because the Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie
-classification replaces a single pumped orbit by a finite paired-loop cover
-of each full representation language. Mignotte's theorem then makes every
-pair of loop images have finite intersection. Retaining the individual
-recurrence shifts, spectral data, and effective Mignotte thresholds gives the

+The affine recurrence action converts one synchronized pumping family into
+an injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Adic topology
+turns those returns into scatteredness and prime-support obstructions, while
+Evertse's quotient theorem and Schur's theorem identify the remaining
+bounded-support possibility as a geometric ray \(cb^t\). In standard
+weak-Perron greedy systems, the length squeeze classifies that possibility
+algebraically: it occurs if and only if a positive power of the weak Perron
+root is an integer.

+For slender context-free languages, a finite paired-loop cover supplies

+each loop to finitely many recurrence sequences, and dominant-root transfer
+followed by Mignotte's theorem gives the two-system Cobham finiteness result.

+the one-system geometric-ray problem, candidate verification is effective,

+witness; this is the missing step toward a general decision procedure.

-\subsection{Relation to prior work}\label{subsec:prior-work}
+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a
+prefix beyond the recurrence transient, every digit acts by an integral
+matrix, and every block matrix is invertible modulo integers coprime to the
+trailing coefficient. The weak pumping lemma of
+Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami supplies one family in which finitely many
+fixed blocks are raised to a common exponent. A common order of their
+matrices in a finite general linear group gives the returns in Main
+Theorem A; positive pumped length and canonical uniqueness give
+distinctness.
 
-The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is classical, due to

-\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}: an infinite \(k\)-MCFL contains one family
-with \(2k\) fixed factors pumped by the same exponent. It says nothing
-about every sufficiently long word, and the corresponding strong pumping

+the alternative between new prime divisors and increasing exceptional
+valuations. In the unit case, the same returns also produce quotient

 \subsection{Organization}
 
-\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} begins with the context-free Zeckendorf
-motivation, develops the recurrent block action and synchronized MCFL orbit,
-proves the local-adic and prime-support consequences, establishes the
-geometric-ray characterization and its effective boundary, and concludes
-with the unit and weak-Perron specializations. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham}

+orbit: the Zeckendorf model, affine recurrence action, prime-support
+obstructions, geometric-ray characterization, and weak-Perron
+classification. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham} develops global rigidity from a
+finite paired-loop cover and proves the two-system theorem and its effective
+cardinality refinement. Both branches use the passage
+\[
+  \text{structured word families}
+  \longrightarrow \text{affine matrix powers}
+  \longrightarrow \text{linear recurrences}

+\begin{remark}[Decision boundary]
   \label{rem:general-decision-interface}
-  The preceding corollary does not yield a decision procedure. To turn

-  instance has a geometric synchronized scheme with fan-out and total
-  constant and pumped-block length at most \(B\). No such compression

-  whether one term of a recurrence vanishes, while Positivity and Ultimate
-  Positivity ask for signs of all or all sufficiently late terms; these
-  problems remain open in unrestricted order
-  \cite{OuaknineWorrell2012,AkshayBazilleGenestVahanwala2024}.

-  matrix equations include undecidable families

+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension
-problem for context-free sequences discussed by Caucal and Le Gonidec
-\cite{CaucalLeGonidec2014}; this paper does not settle it. The weak pumping
-mechanism itself still supplies only one ray inside one infinite MCFL, and
-two representations of the same set may supply unrelated rays with no

+an injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Adic topology
+turns those returns into scatteredness and prime-support obstructions, while
+Evertse's quotient theorem and Schur's theorem identify the remaining
+bounded-support possibility as a geometric ray \(cb^t\). In standard
+weak-Perron greedy systems, the length squeeze classifies that possibility
+algebraically: it occurs if and only if a positive power of the weak Perron

+\begin{maintheorem}[A: synchronized orbit and prime support]

 \[

+\begin{maintheorem}[C: slender context-free Cobham theorem]
+Let \(U\) and \(V\) be strictly increasing standard greedy linear
+numeration sequences whose minimal tail recurrence polynomials are the
+minimal polynomials of weak Perron numbers \(\alpha>1\) and \(\beta>1\).
+If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are multiplicatively independent and both
+\(\operatorname{Rep}_U(X)\) and \(\operatorname{Rep}_V(X)\) are slender
+context-free languages, then \(X\) is finite.
+\end{maintheorem}
 
-There are two resolved regimes. When the trailing coefficient is a unit,
-the synchronized orbit admits quotient congruences of arbitrary prescribed
-depth and an induced copy of the countably branching divisibility tree with
-pairwise coprime, arbitrarily rough edge quotients
-(\Cref{thm:unit-mcfl-deep-congruence-chain,thm:unit-mcfl-divisibility-tree}).
-For standard greedy linear numeration bases with weak-Perron recurrence,

-Charlier--Kreczman obtain residue-class quotient limits for regular

-contribution here is the prime-support/MCFL interface and its exact
-geometric-ray and algebraic classification, not that quotient-limit

+This is \Cref{thm:slender-cfl-cobham}. With complete recurrence and

-A separate two-system result begins from a different language-theoretic
-input. The Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie classification gives a finite paired-loop
-cover of an entire slender context-free language. Combining that global
